basis: per 1000 kg of acetone, the basis of the only quantitative statement in the chapter (sec. 1.5.2, citing Wells 1999)
allocation: None. Acetone and phenol are co-products of the cumene process - 'Acetone and phenol are co-products and their production and demand are intertwined' - and the excerpt states that the cumene figure excludes the phenol ('The production of the co-product phenol is not included in this figure'), i.e. 100 % of the cumene is charged to the acetone. No burden is shifted to phenol here either.

items.name: Cumene
items.quote: Wells (1999) indicates that 2300 kg of cumene are required to produce 1000 kg of acetone with a yield of 90%. The production of the co-product phenol is not included in this figure.
items.note: The only number in the whole chapter that belongs to the unit process rather than to the cumulated vector. It is internally consistent: the cumene cleavage is C6H5C(CH3)2OOH -> C6H5OH + CH3COCH3, so 1 kg of acetone (M = 58.08 g/mol) carries 120.19/58.08 = 2.07 kg of cumene at full conversion, and 2.07/0.90 = 2.30 kg at the 90 % yield the sentence states - exactly the printed 2300 kg per 1000 kg. The figure therefore assigns the whole cumene input to the acetone and none of it to the phenol, which is what the second sentence says.

items.name: Phenol
items.note: Stoichiometric co-product of the same cleavage: 94.11/58.08 = 1.62 kg of phenol per kg of acetone. Recorded for completeness only - the excerpt gives no allocation and explicitly excludes phenol from the cumene figure, so no credit is taken and the whole burden stays with the acetone. (kind = co-product, so it is skipped by the assembler.)

items.name: Sulphuric acid
items.quote: Cumene is oxidised to cumene hydroperoxide (2) which is split to form phenol and acetone (3), using sulphuric acid.
items.note: Named by the excerpt as the cleavage catalyst but never quantified, so per rule 8 it cannot carry an amount; recorded as ignore and repeated in gaps.

items.name: Oxygen / air
items.note: Air oxidation; the excerpt gives the equation but no air or oxygen amount, and ecoinvent does not inventory air.

gaps: Sulphuric acid for the cleavage step: named in the excerpt, never quantified.
Electricity and process heat: the chapter gives reaction conditions (200-250 C and 15-35 bar for the alkylation, 300-450 C and 2-3 bar for the isopropanol route) but no energy figure at all.
Direct emissions: the chapter prints none for the unit process; Tab. 3.2 and Tab. 3.3 are the cumulated vector of the target itself and are deliberately outside the excerpt.
Catalyst, infrastructure and feedstock transport: not mentioned.
The distillation losses and the neutralisation of the residual acid are described qualitatively only.

The route split: the chapter names a second route (dehydrogenation of isopropyl alcohol, 90-95 % yield) and then says the PlasticsEurope data 'assumes that acetone stems from the oxidation of cumene, i.e. the isopropyl alcohol production route is not included in this inventory', so the cumene route is the right one - but no share is given for reality.
